options: A type of Oracle Service Request
The intensive, stabilization-focused support period immediately following go-live
A phase of fit-gap analysis
A quarterly update readiness review
questions.explain: Hypercare is the elevated, intensive support period immediately after go-live, run by the implementation team itself.

questions.q: How does hypercare support typically differ from standard production support?
options: It has slower response times
It is provided exclusively by Oracle Support
It is provided by the implementation team itself with elevated responsiveness, often hours or same-day
It has no defined scope or duration
questions.explain: Hypercare is staffed by the implementation team with much faster response expectations than routine, steady-state support.

questions.q: Why might a project deliberately keep hypercare open through a full month-end close?
options: Because it's the real test of whether modules like GL, AP, AR, and Cash Management close cleanly together under live conditions
Because month-end close is unrelated to the new system
Because Oracle requires it contractually
Because the Executive Sponsor enjoys extended support periods
questions.explain: A full business cycle like month-end close is often used as an exit criterion because it validates that all modules work together correctly under real conditions.

questions.q: What risk comes from ending hypercare on a fixed calendar date alone, regardless of conditions?
options: None — a calendar date is always the best approach
It automatically triggers a quarterly update
It guarantees Severity 1 defects will never occur
Dropping the business right when it still needs elevated support
questions.explain: Ending hypercare by date alone, without checking exit criteria, risks withdrawing support before the business is actually stable.

questions.q: How did Brightfield structure its hypercare period?
options: One day of support with no follow-up
Four weeks, tapering from daily to three-times-weekly stand-ups, staying open through the first month-end close
An indefinite, unscoped support arrangement
Immediate handoff to Oracle Support with no internal involvement
questions.explain: Brightfield's hypercare ran four weeks with tapering stand-up frequency, deliberately extending through the first full month-end close before closing out.
